concept.name: Time-series cross-validation
concept.definition: Cross-validation whose splits preserve chronology so training observations precede the observations used for evaluation.
concept.intuition: It estimates how a fitted choice behaves on observations that were not used to fit that choice.
concept.mechanics: Create sequential train/test index pairs, optionally cap the training window and insert a gap, fit on past rows, and score the next block.
concept.failure_modes: Random splitting, overlapping labels, repeated tuning, or an unprotected final test set can produce optimistic estimates.
concept.misconceptions: Validation measures conditional generalization under a split design; it does not guarantee future market performance.
concept.example: Train on months 1-24 and test 25-30, then train on 1-30 and test 31-36.
